chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, I have transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Mūsā ibn al-Mutawakkil—may Allah be pleased with him—from ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUthmān al-Khazzāz,
and it is said that he was Ibrāhīm ibn ʿĪsā.

key_terms.أَبِي أَيُّوبَ الْخَزَّازِ: Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, the narrator to whom this transmission chain leads
key_terms.الْحِمْيَرِيِّ: A nisbah identifying ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar as al-Ḥimyarī
key_terms.الْمُتَوَكِّلِ: Part of the name Muḥammad ibn Mūsā ibn al-Mutawakkil in the chain
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; a statement indicating the author’s mode of narration

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits narrations from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh. It also records a note about the narrator’s identification, mentioning that he is also said to have been Ibrāhīm ibn ʿĪsā.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah (swt) be pleased with him - from Abdullah ibn Jafar Al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Uthman Al-Khazzaz.
It is also said that his name was Ibrahim ibn Isa.
